To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the efficiency of cationsic lipid-mediated transgene expression is dependent on the DOTMA to DNA or DOTMA to Tween ratio in the lipid formulation.
cationic lipids can efficiently transfect cells in vivo via systemic administration and that the transfection efficiency is dependent upon both DOTMA to lipid ratio and DOTMA to DNA ratios.
the transfection efficiency is determined by both the ratio of DOTAMA to DNA, and the DOTMA to Tween ratio, and that gene expression is transient due to the loss of transgenes from transfected cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the factors controlling the efficiency of the cationic lipid–based delivery system for systemic gene transfer in vivo.
the development and evaluation of cationic liposome-based gene delivery systems.
the development of a nonviral gene therapy system for the treatment of lung diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the factors controlling the transgene expression are the DOTMA to DNA ratios, the DOTMA to Tween ratios and the time of the expression after administration.

the efficiency of cDNA delivery in vivo is dependent on the following factors: the nature of the cDNA to be delivered, the route of administration, the type of carrier used, the ratio of carrier to cDNA, the nature of the carrier, and the animal used.
the efficiency of gene delivery by DOTMA–Tween lipid formulation depends on the ratio of DOTAMA to DNA, DOTAMA to Tween 80 and the amount of DNA administered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cationic liposomes can be used for gene delivery in vivo, and that this can be accomplished by intravenous administration.
cationic liposome-based gene delivery systems are efficient for gene delivery into the lung following systemic administration.

the efficiency of cDNA transfection by DOTMA–Tween lipid formulation is dependent on the DOTMA to DNA as well as DOTMA to Tween ratio in the formulation and that the transgene expression is transient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transfection efficiency can be improved by using the right ratio of cationic lipids to DNA and to Tween 80.
the efficiency of cDNA delivery can be enhanced if the composition of DNA–lipid complex is properly controlled.
it is possible to achieve efficient gene delivery to multiple tissues following intravenous administration of cationic DNA–lipid complex.
